bid event:

bidder.  (Authorization  Letter  in  lieu of  the  same  shall  be  submitted  along with  the  signed  and 
stamped Acceptance Form). 
2.  Tata  Power-DDL  will  make  every  effort  to  make  the  bid  process  transparent.  However,  the 
award decision by Tata Power-DDL would be final and binding on the supplier. 
3.  The  bidder  agrees  to  non-disclosure  of  trade  information  regarding  the  purchase,  identity  of

possibility of non-participation in the auction event.

GUIDING PRINCIPLES FOR SUSTAINABLE PROCUREMENT 
(To be signed and stamped by the bidder) 
To ensure sustainable procurement at TATA Power DDL, It is expected from Business associates to 
integrate  environmental,  social  and  ethical  principles  into  their  businesses  as  per  the  guidelines 
enlisted below. 
1.  Eco friendly transport wherever feasible during execution of the Contract. 
2.  Compliance  to  Statutory  and  regulatory  pollution  norms  like  prevalent  BS  norm,  Pollution 
Certificate etc. 
3.  Formulate a waste management plan and having the waste reduction targets with monitoring. 
4.  Reduction/recycling of all types of  waste during the production lifecycle of material /execution 
of service majorly  
a.  Plastic waste 
b.  E –waste  
c.  Any other non-biodegradable waste 
5.  Responsible  disposal  of  any  hazardous  waste  as  per  Govt.  /Pollution  Control  committee 
guidelines.  
6.  Vendor to use environmentally preferable chemical products if they exist (e.g. low-VOC paints, 
biodegradable cleaning products) and safe lubricants wherever technically feasible. 
7.  Packaging material to be non-hazardous and biodegradable to the extent possible 
8.  Bidders  are  further  advised  to  ensure  reusable  packaging  be  utilized  at  their  end  wherever 
possible during. 
9.  Necessary involvement and development of community through employment creation and skills 
development, technology development and access,  wealth and income  creation, health, social 
investment.  
10. Support the principles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. 
11. Refusal to forced labour. Employees must not be required to submit deposits, money or papers 
with their employer. 
12. Refusal to accept the use of child labour in the supply chain. 
13. A healthy and safe working environment must be provided for all employees, in accordance with 
standards and laws.
